# ==============================================================
# R for Data Science (MSDA9113) - Final Exam - Cholera outbreak
# Data: DataFile.xlsx (line list of cases)
# The code follows the 7 tasks of the exam, in order.
# ==============================================================

# ---- 0. Packages ---------------------------------------------
# Run ONCE if a package is missing:
# install.packages(c("readxl", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "lubridate",
#                    "janitor", "scales"))

library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)
library(janitor)
library(scales)

dir.create("outputs", showWarnings = FALSE)   # folder for figures/tables

# ---- 1. Import the data --------------------------------------
# file.choose() opens a window: click DataFile.xlsx.
# (Or use: read_excel("DataFile.xlsx") if the file is in your working folder)
cholera <- read_excel(file.choose())
cholera <- clean_names(cholera)     # column names -> lower_case_with_underscores

names(cholera)      # look at the real column names
glimpse(cholera)    # structure and data types
head(cholera)

# ---- Auto-detect the important columns ------------------------
# The code searches the column names for key words, then renames them
# to: sex, age, province, district, date_onset, outcome.
find_col <- function(pattern) {
  hit <- grep(pattern, names(cholera), value = TRUE)
  if (length(hit) == 0) NA_character_ else hit[1]
}

col_map <- c(
  sex        = find_col("sex|gender"),
  age        = find_col("^age"),
  province   = find_col("prov"),
  district   = find_col("dist"),
  date_onset = find_col("onset|date"),
  outcome    = find_col("outcome|final|status")
)
print(col_map)   # CHECK: is each new name matched to the right column?

# If something is NA or wrong, set it by hand, for example:
# col_map["outcome"] <- "final_status"

col_map <- col_map[!is.na(col_map)]
cholera <- cholera %>% rename(all_of(col_map))

# ==============================================================
# TASK 1: Identify and list data quality issues
# ==============================================================
cat("Number of rows:", nrow(cholera), "\n")
cat("Duplicated rows:", sum(duplicated(cholera)), "\n")

colSums(is.na(cholera))                  # missing values per column
table(cholera$sex, useNA = "ifany")     # different spellings of sex
table(cholera$outcome, useNA = "ifany") # different spellings of outcome
summary(as.numeric(cholera$age))         # impossible ages?
sum(as.numeric(cholera$age) < 0 | as.numeric(cholera$age) > 110, na.rm = TRUE)
range(cholera$date_onset, na.rm = TRUE)  # impossible dates?

# Write in your report the issues you found, for example:
#  - missing values (age, province, date of onset ...)
#  - duplicated records
#  - sex coded in different ways (M, Male, F, female ...)
#  - wrong data types (age or dates stored as text)
#  - impossible values (negative age, future dates)
#  - inconsistent spelling of provinces, districts, outcome

# ---- Basic cleaning --------------------------------------------
to_date <- function(x) {
  if (is.numeric(x)) as.Date(x, origin = "1899-12-30")  # Excel serial numbers
  else as.Date(x)
}

cholera <- cholera %>%
  distinct() %>%                                        # remove duplicates
  mutate(
    age        = as.numeric(age),
    age        = ifelse(age < 0 | age > 110, NA, age),  # impossible -> NA
    date_onset = to_date(date_onset),
    province   = trimws(province),
    district   = trimws(district)
  )

# ==============================================================
# TASK 2: Harmonize the coding of "Sex"
# ==============================================================
cholera <- cholera %>%
  mutate(
    sex = case_when(
      tolower(trimws(sex)) %in% c("m", "male", "man", "masculin") ~ "Male",
      tolower(trimws(sex)) %in% c("f", "female", "woman", "feminin", "féminin") ~ "Female",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )
table(cholera$sex, useNA = "ifany")    # check: Male / Female / NA only

# ==============================================================
# TASK 3: Recode Age into AgeGroup
# ==============================================================
# right = FALSE: the left value is included, so [5,15) means 5 to 14
cholera <- cholera %>%
  mutate(
    age_group = cut(
      age,
      breaks = c(-Inf, 5, 15, 25, 50, Inf),
      labels = c("Less than 5 years", "5-14 years", "15-24 years",
                 "25-49 years", "50 years and above"),
      right  = FALSE
    )
  )
table(cholera$age_group, useNA = "ifany")

# Outcome -> 1 = died, 0 = recovered (edit the words if your data differ)
cholera <- cholera %>%
  mutate(
    died = case_when(
      tolower(trimws(outcome)) %in% c("died", "dead", "death", "deceased") ~ 1,
      tolower(trimws(outcome)) %in% c("recovered", "alive", "discharged", "cured") ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )
table(cholera$outcome, cholera$died, useNA = "ifany")   # check the recode

# ==============================================================
# TASK 4: Statistical analyses for the Minister of Health
# ==============================================================

# --- 4a. Total number of cases and geographic distribution ---
total_cases <- nrow(cholera)
cat("TOTAL CASES:", total_cases, "\n")

cases_province <- cholera %>%
  count(province, name = "cases") %>%
  mutate(percent = round(cases / sum(cases) * 100, 1)) %>%
  arrange(desc(cases))
print(cases_province)

cases_district <- cholera %>%
  count(province, district, name = "cases") %>%
  arrange(desc(cases))
print(cases_district)

# --- 4b. Number of deaths and Case Fatality Rate (CFR) --------
# CFR (%) = (number of deaths / number of cases) * 100
cfr_province <- cholera %>%
  group_by(province) %>%
  summarise(
    cases   = n(),
    deaths  = sum(died == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    cfr_pct = round(deaths / cases * 100, 1)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(cfr_pct))
print(cfr_province)

overall_cfr <- round(sum(cholera$died == 1, na.rm = TRUE) / total_cases * 100, 1)
cat("OVERALL CFR:", overall_cfr, "%\n")

# --- 4c. Most and least affected age groups (children highlighted)
age_tab <- cholera %>%
  filter(!is.na(age_group)) %>%
  count(age_group, name = "cases") %>%
  mutate(
    percent  = round(cases / sum(cases) * 100, 1),
    children = age_group %in% c("Less than 5 years", "5-14 years")
  )
print(age_tab)
cat("Most affected  :", as.character(age_tab$age_group[which.max(age_tab$cases)]), "\n")
cat("Least affected :", as.character(age_tab$age_group[which.min(age_tab$cases)]), "\n")
cat("Children (<15) :", sum(age_tab$percent[age_tab$children]), "% of cases\n")

fig_age <- ggplot(age_tab, aes(x = age_group, y = cases, fill = children)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(percent, "%")), vjust = -0.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey60", "red3"),
                    labels = c("Adults", "Children (under 15)"), name = "") +
  labs(title = "Cholera cases by age group (children highlighted)",
       x = "Age group", y = "Number of cases") +
  theme_minimal()
print(fig_age)
ggsave("outputs/fig_age_group.png", fig_age, width = 8, height = 5)

# --- 4d. Gender distribution ---------------------------------
sex_tab <- cholera %>%
  filter(!is.na(sex)) %>%
  count(sex, name = "cases") %>%
  mutate(percent = round(cases / sum(cases) * 100, 1))
print(sex_tab)

fig_sex <- ggplot(sex_tab, aes(x = sex, y = cases, fill = sex)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(percent, "%")), vjust = -0.4) +
  labs(title = "Cholera cases by sex", x = "Sex", y = "Number of cases") +
  theme_minimal()
print(fig_sex)
ggsave("outputs/fig_sex.png", fig_sex, width = 6, height = 5)

# --- 4e. Are cases equal across age groups, genders, districts?
# Chi-square goodness-of-fit test.
# H0: cases are equally distributed.  If p < 0.05 -> reject H0.
chisq.test(table(cholera$age_group))
chisq.test(table(cholera$sex))
chisq.test(table(cholera$district))

# --- 4f. Epidemic curve (new cases per day of onset) ----------
epi <- cholera %>%
  filter(!is.na(date_onset)) %>%
  count(date_onset, name = "cases")

fig_epi <- ggplot(epi, aes(x = date_onset, y = cases)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Epidemic curve of the cholera outbreak",
       x = "Date of onset", y = "Number of new cases") +
  theme_minimal()
print(fig_epi)
ggsave("outputs/fig_epidemic_curve.png", fig_epi, width = 9, height = 5)

# --- 4g. Distribution by outcome and recovery rate ------------
outcome_tab <- cholera %>%
  count(outcome, name = "cases") %>%
  mutate(percent = round(cases / sum(cases) * 100, 1))
print(outcome_tab)

recovery_rate <- round(mean(cholera$died == 0, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1)
cat("RECOVERY RATE:", recovery_rate, "%\n")

# ==============================================================
# TASK 5: Figures that show the outbreak situation
# ==============================================================
fig_prov <- ggplot(cases_province, aes(x = reorder(province, cases), y = cases)) +
  geom_col(fill = "darkorange") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Cholera cases by province", x = "Province", y = "Cases") +
  theme_minimal()
print(fig_prov)
ggsave("outputs/fig_province.png", fig_prov, width = 7, height = 4)

fig_cfr <- ggplot(cfr_province, aes(x = reorder(province, cfr_pct), y = cfr_pct)) +
  geom_col(fill = "firebrick") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Case fatality rate by province", x = "Province", y = "CFR (%)") +
  theme_minimal()
print(fig_cfr)
ggsave("outputs/fig_cfr.png", fig_cfr, width = 7, height = 4)

fig_outcome <- ggplot(outcome_tab, aes(x = outcome, y = cases, fill = outcome)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(percent, "%")), vjust = -0.4) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of cases by outcome", x = "Outcome", y = "Cases") +
  theme_minimal()
print(fig_outcome)
ggsave("outputs/fig_outcome.png", fig_outcome, width = 6, height = 5)

# ==============================================================
# TASK 6: Risk factors (estimates and detailed output)
# ==============================================================
# Logistic regression: which factors increase the odds of DEATH?
risk_model <- glm(died ~ age_group + sex + province,
                  data = cholera, family = binomial)
summary(risk_model)

# Odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals
or_table <- exp(cbind(OR = coef(risk_model), confint.default(risk_model)))
print(round(or_table, 2))
write.csv(round(or_table, 2), "outputs/odds_ratios.csv")

# How to read the result:
#  OR > 1 : higher odds of dying than the reference group
#  OR < 1 : lower odds
#  If the 95% CI does not include 1 (or p < 0.05) -> significant risk factor

# Simple association tests with outcome
chisq.test(table(cholera$age_group, cholera$died))
chisq.test(table(cholera$sex, cholera$died))
chisq.test(table(cholera$province, cholera$died))

# ==============================================================
# TASK 7: Recommendations (write them in your own words)
# ==============================================================
#  1. Send teams, ORS, medicines and treatment centres first to the
#     most affected provinces and districts.
#  2. Protect the most affected age groups (children): early care-seeking,
#     community health worker follow-up.
#  3. Improve water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH): chlorination, safe
#     water, latrines, handwashing, safe food.
#  4. Reduce the case fatality rate: train health staff, set up cholera
#     treatment units, keep stocks, create community ORS points.
#  5. Strengthen surveillance: faster reporting, complete data (fewer
#     missing values), standard coding (sex, age, outcome), weekly
#     epidemic curve.
#  6. Consider oral cholera vaccination in hotspot districts and run
#     community awareness campaigns.

# Save the cleaned data
write.csv(cholera, "outputs/cholera_clean.csv", row.names = FALSE)
